For \(x=10\), the base-20 interpretation is \(20\), while twice the base-13 interpretation is \(2\cdot 13=26\), so it is invalid.

Let the decimal digits of \(x\) be \(d_0,d_1,\dots,d_n\). Then
\[
\sum d_i 20^i = 2\sum d_i 13^i
\]
so
\[
\sum d_i(20^i-2\cdot 13^i)=0.
\]
The coefficients are
\[
-1,\ -6,\ 62,\ 3606,\ 102878,\dots
\]
Thus
\[
d_0+6d_1=62d_2+3606d_3+\cdots.
\]
Since \(d_i\le 9\), the left side is at most \(9+54=63\). The only possible positive right side within this bound is \(62\), so \(d_2=1\) and all higher digits are \(0\). Then
\[
d_0+6d_1=62.
\]
With digits \(0\le d_0,d_1\le 9\), the only solution is \(d_0=8,\ d_1=9\). Therefore
\[
x=198.
\]

\[
\boxed{198}
\]
